newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht still in demand, ringgit rises.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht still in demand, ringgit rises.

text.p: The Thai baht remained well bid in offshore markets on Friday as players continued to unload the dollar to cover their short baht positions, dealers said.
But they said the pace of buying had slowed somewhat and some profit-taking interest was seen below the 24.00 level to the dollar.
"Most of the dollar/baht selling was done yesterday for the maturity on June 9 of some outright forward positions taken a month ago," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.
The baht jumped to a high of 23.800/24.000 to the dollar offshore on Thursday, its highest level since being devalued in 1984.
On Friday, the Thai unit remained strong, hitting a high of 23.750 in early trade. It was quoted at 23.750/23.850 at 0425 GMT compared with 24.00/24.10 late on Thursday.

Dealers said trade in offshore markets was still confined to participants selling dollars for baht as swaps remained very high in the face of the Thai central bank's continued restrictions on offshore lending by domestic banks.

A two-tier baht market has been in place since mid-May when speculative attacks on the currency prompted the central bank to impose what dealers called capital controls to cut off baht supply to offshore players.
The one-month swap premium was traded at 130/160 satangs per dollar in offshore markets and 18/23 onshore. It was at around 6-10 satangs before the two-tier baht market developed.
"The market is still waiting to sell the dollar on any rally. It's driven by supply and demand conditions," the Singapore dealer said.
"Eventually, dollar/baht may drift down to test 23.00 or maybe much lower, depending on the trade-off between the Bank of Thailand and the speculators," he added.
Research firm I.D.E.A. said in a daily commentary that more turbulence in the baht was on the cards as offshore funds were still very long on the spot dollar/baht outright.
"A substantial portion of next week maturities are with banks in Thailand. This means further drain of liquidity from the cash-strapped offshore market," it said.
Any leftward shift in the forward market would represent opportunities to go long the dollar/baht forwards again, it said.
In Malaysia, the ringgit rose suddenly as buying of the ringgit/Singapore dollar cross by U.S. investment houses triggered stop-loss dollar sales around the 2.5140 level.
"The investment houses bought ringgit/Sing in good size, easily around $50-100 million. So dollar/ringgit was sold around 2.5160," the Singapore-based dealer said.
He said the market was taken off guard when dollar/ringgit fell below 2.5140 as it had traded a 2.5145-2.5180 range for the past two weeks.
Corporate dollar demand out of Kuala Lumpur blocked the ringgit's rise and the currency was now likely to trade a new 2.5100-2.5150 range to the dollar, he said.
The ringgit was at 2.5127/37 to the dollar at 0425 GMT against 2.5160/70 at the Kuala Lumpur close on Thursday.
The Singapore dollar came under some pressure from the ringgit/Sing buying but domestic corporate demand for the unit limited its decline.
"Local corporates are looking to sell dollar/Sing from 1.4300 to 1.4320, so any upmoves will be very slow," a dealer said.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was relatively steady in slow trade amid adequate money market liquidity with dollar selling interest seen above the 2,430 level, dealers said.

They said the market was awaiting a decision by the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) on whether it would accept the results of last week's general election. The party was due to make a statement around 0700 GMT.
A European bank dealer in Jakarta said offshore players continued to maintain long positions in forwards and short on dollars in the spot market, triggering a slew of tom/next unwinding.
Dealers said concerns about a Thai-style funding squeeze lingered in the Jakarta forward market, despite Bank Indonesia's denial that it would implement measures mirroring the Bank of Thailand.
The rupiah was well capped at the resistance level of 2,430 due to local selling and foreign buying, keeping the spot rate in a narrow range of 2,429 and 2,430 on Friday.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
